newsitem.title: ISRAEL: ESC Medical sees merger speeding growth.
newsitem.headline: ESC Medical sees merger speeding growth.

text.p: Israel's ESC Medical Systems Ltd, a maker of cosmetic-surgery lasers, expects faster sales growth in the key U.S. market by merging with Seattle-based Luxar Corp, ESC president Shimon Eckhouse said on Tuesday.
"Luxar's installed based give us immediate access to a very large market," Eckhouse told Reuters.
"We have a sales force in the U.S. that is relatively small. This gives us a presence in our most important market," he said.
ESC, based in Yokneam in northern Israel, said last week the merger would be carried out via an issue of 2.5 million new shares to closely-held Luxar in a pooling of interests.
Luxar will become a subsidiary of the Israeli company and its shareholders will hold a 12.3 percent stake in ESC after dilution, Eckhouse said.
With ESC shares closing in Monday Nasdaq trading at $35, the transaction is valued at $87.5 million at today's prices. ESC said the two sides expected to complete the merger by March 19.

Eckhouse, which in June 1996 acquired another medical-laser maker called LBT Ltd, said ESC was on the lookout for other mergers and acquisitions. "I would say that this is part of our basic strategy," he said.

The two companies have complementary product lines, with both of them developing, manufacturing and marketing laser devices used principally for cosmetic surgery in private clinics rather than hospitals.
"They (Luxar) have developed two major products being sold now," said Eckhouse.

"One is a CO2 laser, which is used in skin re-surfacing in private medical clinics. We look at it as the ideal product for office-based cosmetic surgery," he said. "The other is a CO2 laser for applications in dentistry, ENT, oral surgery and so on -- again ideally suited for office procedures."
ESC's principal product, PhotDermVL, is used for treating varicose veins and other benign vascular lesions. Other products treat pigmented lesions and skin tumours and resurface skin.

Luxor brings to the deal an installed based in the United States of over 3,000 lasers, a 65-strong U.S. sales force, and international distributors. ESC, whose first product was launched in 1995, has only 15 sales people and an installed based of 400 units.
Eckhouse said Luxor's installed based was important because he expected Luxor customers would also buy ESC equipment.

Luxar, founded in 1988, had net sales of $28.1 million in the year ended September 30, 1996, close to ESC's $32.9 million for calendar 1996. But the Seattle company reported net earnings of just $4.5 million against ESC's $12.7 million.
Eckhouse said the deal was structured so that per share earnings would not be hurt. He added that the merged companies would achieve some savings from combined marketing and research.
Luxar also brings two new products with it, one for teeth whitening and another for reducing cellulite, or fat that is considered resistant to dieting, Eckhouse said.
